findings.message: B-01 (NEW, sources). fig-U3-7 asserts an unverified sample size that the unit's own prose says is unstated, and it is live on a page published to learners. Locator: static/img/figures/efmp-302/unit-03/fig-U3-7.svg and fig-U3-7.dark.svg, the class="m" text node at x=20 y=344, reading verbatim: "Furlich (2016), N=77: the verbal measure was significant, the non-verbal one was not." The figure is carried by docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-03/topic-04.mdx:26 (<Figure id="fig-U3-7" .../>) and renders on /semester-1/efmp-302/unit-03/topic-04/. The bound excerpt specs/content/efmp-302/sources/texts/furlich2016.md:22-24 states in its own scope note: "The abstract does NOT state the sample size. Unit 3 prose cites 'N=77'; that figure is not confirmed by this excerpt and needs the full text or the methods section to verify." The same topic's prose at topic-04.mdx:120-121 now says the opposite of the figure: "The published abstract gives neither a sample size nor a country, so treat both as unstated rather than small and American", and Further reading at :256-257 repeats it. So the unit simultaneously tells a learner that no sample size is available and shows one, in the same topic, with the figure carrying the attribution. WHY FIVE PRIOR RUNS MISSED IT: the run-002 blocking finding on N=77 was closed in runs 003/004/005 on the strength of a grep restricted to docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-03/ (run004's own evidence string says so verbatim). Figure text lives in static/img/figures/efmp-302/unit-03/, which that grep never reached, and check:figures validates the manifest, carrier and alt text rather than the SVG's caption bytes. REPAIR: delete ", N=77" from the class="m" caption in BOTH fig-U3-7.svg and fig-U3-7.dark.svg, leaving "Furlich (2016): the verbal measure was significant, the non-verbal one was not.", which the bound verbatim abstract supports exactly; then re-run figures:variants:check. Do not add a sample size unless the methods passage is bound.

B-02 (NEW, pedagogy; conflicts with the assessment bank). fig-U3-7 states the channel-contradiction heuristic as established fact, in the one topic whose stated purpose is to refuse exactly that. Locator: static/img/figures/efmp-302/unit-03/fig-U3-7.svg and fig-U3-7.dark.svg, table row 4. The row header (class="rh", x=30 y=274/294) reads "When they contradict each other" and the cell (class="h", bold, x=540 y=272) reads, unqualified: "The class believes the non-verbal channel." The figure's only citation line sits directly beneath it, so the assertion reads as sourced. The carrying topic says the reverse at docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-03/topic-04.mdx:128-140: the claim "comes from the same small experiments" as the 93% claim, "Discarding the number while keeping the conclusion drawn from it would be the same citation failure wearing better clothes", and "treat it as what it is: a practitioner's heuristic ... not established for classroom instruction by the evidence cited in this topic. It is not worth asserting as a research finding". topic-04.mdx:205-206 and the unit summary at unit-assessment.mdx:44-46 say the same. ASSESSMENT CONFLICT: unit-assessment.mdx MCQ 8 asks how that claim is "best described"; the key is b, "a practitioner's heuristic that descends from the same experiments as the 93% claim", and distractor a is "an established finding of the studies cited in this unit". fig-U3-7 is the opening visual of the topic that teaches this item and it supports distractor a. A learner who studies the figure is led to the answer the bank marks wrong. docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-03/unit-teacher-notes.mdx:42-46 makes this the unit's showcase for citation discipline "because the book applies the rule to itself"; here it does not. REPAIR: qualify the row in BOTH SVG variants, e.g. cell text "The class usually believes the non-verbal channel." with the class="m" sub-line changed to carry "Practitioner's heuristic, not a finding of the study cited below."; keep the existing "take your time / glancing at the clock" illustration if it fits. Re-run figures:variants:check and measure-figure-text.mjs afterwards, since both edits change text width.

A-01 (NEW, accessibility/presentation). fig-U3-6's wordmark is overprinted by an outcome box, in both committed variants, and no gate sees it. static/img/figures/efmp-302/unit-03/fig-U3-6.svg and fig-U3-6.dark.svg: rect.o2, the "Escalated to the head" outcome box, occupies [640,440,850,504]; the class="wm" text "textbook.com.pk" occupies [775.7,493.6,868.6,506.8]. Measured overlap 74.3 x 10.4 px. The wordmark is later in document order so it paints over the box, and the box's bottom stroke at y=504 runs through the glyphs. Captured at 3x in specs/content/efmp-302/reviews/unit-03/renders-agent-g3-efmp302-u3-run007/fig-U3-6-wordmark-collision-3x.png and visible in the A4 print render specs/content/efmp-302/reviews/unit-03/renders-agent-g3-efmp302-u3-run007/topic-03-print-A4.png. NOT a blocking defect: the instructional labels are untouched and legible, and the wordmark is aria-hidden="true" branding, so no instructional meaning is lost. Recorded because the G3 reference now directs reviewers to node scripts/measure-figure-text.mjs for exactly this class of defect and that tool does not catch it: scripts/measure-figure-text.mjs:60-70 compares the .wm text box only against other <text> boxes, so a <rect> or <path> over the wordmark passes at exit 0, as it did here (measure-figure-text.log). REPAIR (figure): raise the wordmark, or shorten rect.o2 to end at x<=770, or move the outcome box up. REPAIR (tool, separate and for the owner): extend measure-figure-text.mjs to test painted shapes against the wordmark box, not only text.

A-02 (NEW, pedagogy). fig-U3-3 gives resilience a different excess failure from the prose that the mark scheme keys on. The figure's "How it fails when overdone" cell for Resilience reads "Endures what should be reported"; docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-03/topic-02.mdx:120-122 teaches "Overdone, it becomes stubbornness: persisting with a method for four years because giving it up would feel like defeat." These are different failure modes, not paraphrases: one is tolerating something that ought to be escalated, the other is refusing to abandon a method. unit-assessment.mdx RRQ 4 awards a mark for the failure mode of each chosen trait and the model answer follows the prose. A candidate who revised from the figure gives an answer the scheme does not list. REPAIR: align the fig-U3-3 Resilience cell with the prose, or add the second failure mode to topic-02.mdx and to the RRQ 4 scheme.

A-03 (NEW, pedagogy). fig-U3-5's link labels give illustrative instances where the prose and the RRQ 5 mark scheme require purposes, although the figure's own footnote claims otherwise ("Each link is labelled with what the relationship is FOR"). Figure: colleagues "so a hard class can be handed over"; head teacher "so a problem is heard early"; parents "so a parent will act at home"; community "so a girl is allowed to keep attending". Prose (docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-03/topic-03.mdx:56-76) and the unit-assessment.mdx RRQ 5 scheme require: colleagues "so practice improves and handling is consistent"; institution "so things can be authorised and concerns heard"; parents "so action happens at home AND the teacher learns what they cannot see"; community "so the school can ask things of it". Only the pupils link matches. RRQ 5 is a five-mark recall item scored one per relationship, and fig-U3-5 is the opening visual of the topic it examines. REPAIR: bring the four labels into line with the prose, or widen the RRQ 5 scheme to credit the figure's wording.

A-04 (NEW, readability). fig-U3-9's closing caption says "A teacher today is still expected to transmit content accurately and still expected to instruct - while also doing the three that came after." No count of three fits: the timeline has four stations (Transmitter, Instructor, Facilitator, "And also, now"), so two stations come after Instructor, the "And also, now" box lists four roles, and the unit teaches five roles overall. REPAIR: state the count the figure actually shows, or drop the number.

A-05 (NEW, process; outside the unit but it endangers future reviews of it). review-ref/ is an untracked, git-ignored full-repository snapshot (.gitignore:81) that shadows every bound path with older bytes. Comparing it against this run's manifest: of the 108 bound paths that exist inside it, 36 differ, including docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-03/topic-01.mdx through topic-05.mdx, unit-assessment.mdx, specs/content/efmp-302/sources/unit-03.md, coverage/unit-03.md, figures/unit-03.md, content-spec.md, the constitution, the review skill and g3.md itself. Because it is git-ignored it never enters the manifest and prepare() never reports it as dirty, so nothing in the evidence contract warns a reviewer off it. A reviewer who opens review-ref/docs/... reviews superseded content and would validate cleanly against the current manifest regardless. RECORDED, not repaired: the reviewer does not delete files. REPAIR for the owner: remove the snapshot, or move it outside the working tree.

A-09 (carried from run-005 F-04, re-verified and extended). U3-11's grounding is nominal in the prose, and two declared-unretrievable sources are attributed without a point-of-use scope note. specs/content/efmp-302/coverage/unit-03.md grounds U3-11 in brookfield2017, but topic-05.mdx:42-70, the "### The teacher as facilitator and as researcher" section, carries no Brookfield citation; Brookfield's only topic-05 citation is at :105, inside "### The teacher as life-long learner", which coverage grounds in suarez2022. Separately, and beyond what run 005 recorded: hurst2009 and brookfield2017 are both declared under "## Unverifiable sources" as unread ("supported at bibliographic level only"), yet topic-02.mdx:48-52 attributes a specific list to Hurst and Reding ("punctuality, preparedness, the willingness to be interrupted by a pupil's question, follow-through on what was promised") and topic-05.mdx:105-108 attributes a comparative claim to Brookfield ("development that consists of collecting courses is weaker than ..."), neither marked as uncorroborated at the point of use. ASSESSED AGAINST THE AMENDED RUBRIC AND NOT FAILED: g3.md's test is "whether the declaration is honest and complete, not whether the text was obtained", and specs/content/efmp-302/sources/unit-03.md is honest and complete here - it names the level of support, names the exact sub-topic set each key grounds, and volunteers that "U3-11, the researcher role, rests on this unread source alone". The attributions are general characterisations of well-known works rather than statistics or reported findings, so they do not "state more than the declaration supports" in the sense D-2026-0001 limits. Recorded so the owner can decide whether the Unit 6 hennessy2022 model (a "Level of support" line plus a point-of-use note in the prose) should apply here too. REPAIR options for the owner: reground U3-11 as no-external-source as U3-12 was; or cite Brookfield in that section once the book is obtainable; or add point-of-use scope notes.

Measured on the <table> and <figure> elements themselves, every scroll region in the unit reaches its right edge and carries tabindex="0", role="region" and an aria-label, while the wrapper correctly reports overflow-x visible - the reading three earlier reviews mistook for a defect.
